messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: release=v2.14.7 canary=5% region=us-west-2 ts=2026-03-16T23:02:47Z • dashboard: https://console/release/3751234567

sarah: Observability: p95 gen latency jumped 120ms -> 980ms on canary hosts, error rate +1.8% (503/504). Noted at 23:05Z.

mike: I just got paged by the latency alert. Paging group oncall? @lee-oncall are you on?

lee-oncall: oncall here, looking. Can we pin canary to 0% traffic immediately? If deploy has a kill-switch/flag, flip it.

deploy-bot: Action: feature-flag kill-switch applied -> canary traffic set to 0%. rollout.set(canary,0) executed by ci-pipeline. Current canary_traffic=0%

jordan: Even after traffic set to 0, baseline hosts show elevated p95 for async gen paths. I'm seeing kernel fallback logs on the new binary: "kernel_select: fallback -> attention_matmul_generic"

infra-bot: Log snippet from host r-i-03a2:
```
2026-03-16T23:04:58Z kernel_select INFO fallback to matmul_generic (reason=unsupported_optimized_kernel)
2026-03-16T23:05:01Z kv_cache WARN miss_rate=0.42
2026-03-16T23:05:07Z batch_window INFO window_ms=14 -> 48
```

mike: Throughput on canary cohort dropped ~30% before we killed traffic. Batch window jumped and KV cache miss rate spiked ~40%. My hunch: change in batching header or cache key serialization in v2.14.7.

sarah: Customer impact: support reported increased client retries for ~6 customers (SLA threshold crossings). Support team notified and triage initiated. No broad outage but latency hits are user-visible.

lee-oncall: Initiating rollback to v2.14.6 now (canary group). ETA ~8m. Also pushing node-level kernel-affinity revert on affected hosts to prefer optimized kernels. Will monitor p95.

deploy-bot: Rollback started: target=v2.14.6 scope=canary ts=2026-03-16T23:09:12Z. Progress endpoints: https://console/rollback/3751234567

jordan: Preparing a revert patch that restores previous batching key and prevents the kernel selection change. If rollback doesn't return p95 to baseline within 10m we'll trigger a fast patch release.

lee-oncall: Handoff: I'm owning this incident. If p95 > 200ms in 10m escalate to eng-runtime. @mike @jordan please standby for hotfix testing. I'll coordinate customer comms with Sarah after stabilization.

sarah: I'll open the incident doc now and populate initial timeline + customer list. Early hypothesis: batching window calc + kernel-selection heuristics in v2.14.7 caused increased CPU and cache thrash.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed: target=v2.14.6; canary traffic restored to baseline. Metrics: p95 returned to ~140ms, error rate back to baseline. Monitoring set to watch for 30m.

lee-oncall: Confirming metrics look stable. Closing active paging but leaving incident in monitoring watch. Postmortem owner: sarah.
